content:
- Overestimate prices after strong positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot in bullish phases.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or neutral; model fails to adjust downward quickly.
- Lag in downward corrections: model often holds high forecasts even as sentiment turns negative.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs and fails to revert to historical mean when sentiment weakens.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; underperform when sentiment is volatile or mixed.
- Avoid overconfidence in rising sentiment: if sentiment is >0.7 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast slope to avoid overcorrection.
- When sentiment is low (<0.3) and price is falling, model often undercorrects — add 5–10% buffer to downward forecasts.
